details: For real x and t, the predicates x ≥ t and x < t are the two cases used in the decomposition (PDF page 4, printed page 8; first displayed identity).

Under the book’s indicator convention, exactly the term corresponding to the true threshold predicate contributes x, while the other contributes 0 (PDF page 3, printed page 7, footnote 4; and PDF page 4, printed page 8, first displayed identity).
The proof fixes t > 0 before stating the identity, so positivity is inherited even though it is not repeated inside the displayed formula (PDF page 4, printed page 8; anchor: “Fix t > 0”).

undebatable_constraints: The scalar binder x ranges over all real numbers, not merely non-negative reals (PDF page 4, printed page 8; anchor: “any real number x”).
The threshold t is positive in the inherited proof context (PDF page 4, printed page 8; anchor: “Fix t > 0”).
The comparison cases are x ≥ t and x < t, with the boundary x = t included in the first indicator (PDF page 4, printed page 8; first displayed identity).
Indicators must have the book’s 0-or-1 semantics (PDF page 3, printed page 7; footnote 4).

The conclusion is equality of real scalars and is limited to x = x·1_{x≥t} + x·1_{x<t}; later substitution, expectation, and inequality steps are excluded (PDF page 4, printed page 8; first displayed identity and following paragraph).
contract_plain_english: In the proof of Proposition 1.2.4, after fixing a real threshold t > 0, the source states that every real number x equals the sum of x restricted by the indicator of x ≥ t and x restricted by the indicator of x < t. The indicators are 1 when their predicates hold and 0 otherwise. This contract covers only that scalar decomposition, not the later substitution of a random variable, expectation calculation, inequalities, or Markov bound (PDF page 4, printed page 8; with the indicator convention in footnote 4 on PDF page 3, printed page 7).
